raw_segments.text: Let us then consider, first of all, what will be their way of life, now that we have thus
Will they not produce corn and wine and clothes and shoes and build houses for themselves?
And when they are housed, they will work in summer, commonly, stripped and barefoot, but
in winter substantially clothed and shod.
They will feed on barley meal and flour of wheat, baking and kneading them, making noble
These, they will serve up on a mat of reeds or on clean leaves, themselves reclining the
while upon beds strewn with yew or myrtle.
And they and their children will feast, drinking of the wine which they have made, wearing
garlands on their heads and hemming the praises of the gods in happy converse with one another.
